findings.issue_text: [BUG] runShardSplitQuery calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables with a third argument (request.filters) that the method's signature does not accept. LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables is declared as (query: LokiQuery, scopedVars: ScopedVars) => LokiQuery; passing request.filters is a TS2554 too-many-arguments compile error, breaking the Loki datasource build and every CI type-check job on this branch. The diff provides no change to the datasource signature accepting filters, so the call site is invalid as written.

[BUG] runSplitQuery applies template variables to queries without clearing/normalizing downstream fields, unlike the prior shard path which used interpolateVariablesInQueries which also sets intervalMs and maxDataPoints via template interop. Metric queries routed through runSplitQuery previously reached execution with variables already replaced upstream by the datasource's query() path; the new in-place applyTemplateVariables here mutates the shared request.targets objects (applyTemplateVariables returns the same query object it mutates in Loki's implementation), so subsequent consumers of the original request (partial-update bookkeeping, non-splitting query list) observe interpolated state — behavior change with no upstream test asserting idempotency when both the datasource and runSplitQuery interpolate the same target.

[ADVISORY] The new `request.filters` (ad-hoc filters) argument passed to `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` has no test coverage anywhere in the diff — both new 'Interpolates queries before execution' tests only exercise `replace`/`getVariables` and never assert that filters are forwarded to applyTemplateVariables. A regression that drops or misapplies ad-hoc filters on the split-query path (e.g. someone removing the third argument) passes the entire new test suite, and users with ad-hoc filters attached to their Loki datasource get unfiltered split queries returning wrong data.

[ADVISORY] The new interpolation test in querySplitting.test.ts only asserts `mock.calls[0][0].targets[0]` — the first request's first target — while runSplitQuery emits multiple chunked requests for a 3-day range; interpolation of the later chunk requests is unverified. If a future change to the chunk-splitting path rebuilds derived queries from the raw (un-interpolated) target instead of the mapped one, the test still passes because only the first chunk's expr/step is asserted, and long-range dashboards silently send `$__auto`/`$step` literals to Loki on chunks 2..n.

[ADVISORY] The updated 'Interpolates queries before running' test pins `applyTemplateVariables` to exactly 5 calls for a single target, revealing the method is invoked both in the new top-level map and again per sharded query inside the (unshown) splitting pipeline — the diff adds a double-interpolation with no test asserting it is idempotent. Any non-idempotent template (e.g. a custom variable whose `replace` appends rather than substitutes, or `$__auto` resolved relative to prior state) is applied twice to the same expr; a maintainer changing the replace semantics gets doubled substitutions like `{a="b5m5m"}` sent to Loki with no test failure.

[ADVISORY] runShardSplitQuery now interpolates each target via applyTemplateVariables at entry, while the updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' still expects 5 applyTemplateVariables calls for a single-query request, proving the shard-splitting internals also interpolate the already-interpolated queries. Template interpolation runs twice on the same expr; any non-idempotent substitution (a variable whose value contains '$', chained/nested variables, or format modifiers) produces a corrupted selector sent to Loki. Whoever uses shard splitting with such variables gets wrong or empty results.

[ADVISORY] runSplitQuery adds interpolation with no counterpart change to the non-splitting execution path shown in the diff, so the change is only traceable to the new tests, not to any stated requirement about where interpolation belongs. If the surrounding query pipeline already interpolates before invoking runSplitQuery (as the Loki datasource does for direct queries), queries taking the split path are interpolated twice; maintainers bitten by a variable rendering bug will find two interpolation sites to reconcile.

[BUG] The new `map` over `applyTemplateVariables` double-interpolates every query on the shard path, because `splitQueriesByStreamShard` already interpolates each split query again before dispatching it. The PR's own test proves it: with one query in the request, the mock records 5 calls to `applyTemplateVariables` (1 from the new map + 4 per-shard calls inside `splitQueriesByStreamShard` for '5 shards, 3 groups + empty shard group, 4 requests'). Any variable whose interpolated value itself contains variable-like syntax — e.g. a variable holding a label-filter regex with `$`, or a value containing `${...}` text — gets re-expanded on the second pass, silently producing a different expr than the user authored. The tests only pass because `$SELECTOR`/`$__auto`/`$step` replacements are idempotent.

[ADVISORY] runSplitQuery now unconditionally interpolates targets, but the Loki datasource's main `query()` entry point also interpolates targets before dispatch, so queries reaching the split path from the normal pipeline get interpolated twice. If `LokiDatasource.query()` (the production caller of runSplitQuery/runShardSplitQuery) already calls `interpolateVariablesInQueries`/`applyTemplateVariables` on `request.targets` before delegating, this map is a second pass over already-interpolated strings. The tests only exercise runSplitQuery called directly with raw targets, so the double-interpolation behavior in the real entry path is untested and any variable value containing `$`-patterns from user data gets silently mangled. Needs verification that the split entry point is only ever reached with un-interpolated targets (e.g. called before the query()-level interpolation), which this diff does not establish.

[ADVISORY] Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` mutates the target in place and returns it, so the new `map` inside a filter/map pipeline side-effects the caller's `request.targets` objects rather than producing independent interpolated copies. The original `DataQueryRequest` handed to runShardSplitQuery is silently mutated — any later consumer of `request.targets` (retry logic, query editor state, the non-splitting fallback path) now sees interpolated expr/step values, and if the same request object is ever re-dispatched the interpolation compounds. The previous `interpolateVariablesInQueries` had the same mutation habit, but the diff spreads it to the runSplitQuery path too; a shallow copy (`{...query, expr: ...}`) would confine the effect to the split pipeline.

[ADVISORY] The interpolation entry point was silently swapped from interpolateVariablesInQueries to applyTemplateVariables without any evidence the semantic differences were accepted. interpolateVariablesInQueries and applyTemplateVariables are not equivalent: the batch method historically applies datasource-specific formatting/defaults (e.g., string-formatting of variable arrays into LogQL-appropriate form) per query, while applyTemplateVariables applies a single-query path. Users whose $SELECTOR expands to a multi-valued variable now get different (potentially unquoted or non-alternation) expansion in the shard-split path than in every other Loki code path, producing queries Loki rejects or wrong shard selectors — a behavior change inside a PR titled 'Advanced Query Processing Architecture' with no acceptance of the interpolation swap.

[ADVISORY] runSplitQuery now interpolates queries before splitting, but the same queries are still handed to datasource.runQuery, which interpolates again on its normal path — introducing double template-variable application that never existed for this code path. Previously runSplitQuery deliberately passed raw exprs through and let the execution layer interpolate exactly once; after this change any query where interpolation is not idempotent (escaped variables like $${var}, nested ${a${b}} forms, or $step formats like $__rate_interval whose second pass re-expands against the already-substituted range) is interpolated twice, yielding corrupted exprs for users of split queries. The test added in this diff only asserts the happy-path single-pass idempotent case ('$step' -> '5m' -> '5m'), so the drift is unverified.

[ADVISORY] Hidden-query handling order changed relative to the prior accepted behavior: interpolation previously ran on all targets before hide-filtering, now hidden targets are filtered before interpolation. The observable contract change is that request.filters/scopedVars are no longer applied to hidden queries in the shard path; anyone relying on the prior side-effecting interpolation mock (which mutated queries in place) or on hidden queries carrying interpolated exprs downstream sees different state. In the real (non-mutating) datasource this is mostly benign, but the shuffle of filter/map/interpolate ordering happened with no test or note acknowledging it, which is exactly the kind of silent objective drift this lens blocks.

[ADVISORY] The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test asserts interpolation only on the first runQuery call's first target, leaving later split-chunk calls unverified. If applyTemplateVariables were applied to only the first query or first time-chunk (e.g., a regression where later chunks re-use the raw un-interpolated expr), the test still passes because mock.calls[1..n] are never inspected; a user with $__auto in a 3-day query would get 'parse error at 1:1' from Loki on chunks 2+ while CI stays green.

[ADVISORY] The new shard test verifies interpolation and step substitution only on mock.calls[0], though shard splitting issues multiple runQuery calls (the neighboring test documents 4 requests). A regression where interpolation is dropped for all but the first shard-group request passes the test; operators on sharded dashboards get un-interpolated $__auto/$step sent to Loki on shards 2..4 with a green build.

[ADVISORY] The updated 'Interpolates queries before running' test asserts only the mock's invocation count (toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)) for applyTemplateVariables, not that the interpolated results propagate to the actual runQuery payloads. The count assertion verifies the mock was invoked, not the behavior — if the pipeline dropped the returned query objects and executed the raw request.targets instead, the count check still passes while users see un-interpolated expressions; the toHaveBeenCalledWith runQuery assertion that follows partially mitigates this only for one call shape.
